$comment: Neutral shipped <stdint.h> (C99 7.18) — exact-width, minimum-width, fastest-minimum-width, pointer-width, and greatest-width integer typedefs expressed as language-NEUTRAL hir-text aliases, injected by the semantic phase (a C `.h` would be C-syntax TEXT and couple the shipped config to C; see README + limits.json). FIRST real consumer of the FC14 typedef-injection path. The pointer-width forms (intptr_t/uintptr_t) and the greatest-width forms (intmax_t/uintmax_t) are 8 bytes on EVERY current DSS target — all are 64-bit, and LP64 + LLP64 agree on pointer width (only `long` differs, which stdint does not expose) — so they are u64/i64. An ILP32 target would make them 4-byte: deferred D-FFI-STDINT-PTR-WIDTH-ILP32. The fastest-minimum-width forms are implementation-defined; mapping them to their exact-width minimum (int_fast16_t -> i16) is conforming (>= N bits) and keeps SQLite's self-contained amalgamation internally consistent. No `symbols` (no link surface). ★ c82 (shell.c `N==INT64_MIN ? INT64_MAX : -N`) shipped the FIRST slice of the C99 7.18.2 limit macros on `constants`: INT64_MIN/INT64_MAX. ★ P68 round 9 (D-C-LIMITS-H-DEFINES-NINE-OF-THE-STANDARD-MACROS): they were fixed numbers typed a bare `i64`, and C gives each limit macro the type an object of ITS typedef has after promotion (C99 7.18.2p2; C23 7.22.5, by 5.2.5.3) — which is `long` on ELF and `long long` on Mach-O and pe, because `int64_t` is (see the identity record below). They are now `{ "of": "int64_t", "limit": "min" | "max" }`: realized per pair from the `int64_t` typedef this very file declares, by the ONE derived-constant decode `<limits.h>` uses, and spelled by the typed splice with the literal whose phase-7 type IS that type (`9223372036854775807L` on ELF, `9223372036854775807LL` elsewhere). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: `_Generic(INT64_MAX, int64_t: 1, default: 0)` is 1 under gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (x86_64 Linux, and aarch64 Linux under qemu and natively), mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 14.51. ★ P68 round 9 (D-FFI-STDINT-LIMIT-MACROS): THE WHOLE C23 7.22.2 / 7.22.3 FAMILY IS HERE, 84 rows, EVERY ONE A TYPE AND A LIMIT, NONE A NUMBER — the `_MIN`/`_MAX`/`_WIDTH` of each exact-, least-, fast-, pointer- and greatest-width typedef this file declares (`of` the bare typedef name), and of the five types C 7.22.3 takes from OTHER headers, none of which `<stdint.h>` includes: `ptrdiff_t`, `size_t` and `wchar_t` from `<stddef.h>` and `sig_atomic_t` from `<signal.h>` (`of: { "shippedTypedef": …, "header": … }`), and `wint_t` from the target’s platform ABI table (`of: { "abiTypedef": "wint_t" }`) — the SAME references the `__SIZE_MAX__`/`__WINT_MAX__` predefined macros make, read by the same `readShippedHeaderTypedefs` and realized by the same `deriveIntegerLimitOnPair`, so `SIZE_MAX` and `__SIZE_MAX__` cannot disagree on a pair. C 7.22.5 (by 5.2.5.3) gives each `_MIN`/`_MAX` its type’s PROMOTED type — `UINT16_MAX` is an `int`, `UINT32_MAX` an `unsigned int`, `INT_FAST16_MAX` a `long` on ELF — and a type of unspecified signedness that is unsigned there (`wchar_t` on aarch64 Linux, `wint_t` on Linux and Windows) gets a `_MIN` of 0 in that promoted type; each `_WIDTH` is an `int`. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24 by `_Generic` type + printed value + four `#if` predicates per name, after `#include <stdint.h>` alone: gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` and clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` define all 84 with exactly these types and values on x86_64 and aarch64 Linux (the two arches differ only in `WCHAR_MIN`/`WCHAR_MAX`: `int` and signed on x86_64, `unsigned int` and 0 on aarch64). mingw-w64 13.2.0, MSVC 14.51 and Apple clang 21.0.0 (arm64 and `-arch x86_64` identical, MEASURED on the coordinator’s Mac, every `#if` value equal to its C value, each type the promoted type of Darwin’s own typedef) define the 51 `_MIN`/`_MAX` names and NO `_WIDTH` (all 33 absent) — C23 requires those (7.22.2, 7.22.3), so the union includes them — and each deviates from the standard’s TYPES where it deviates from the other: mingw-w64 types `WCHAR_MIN`/`WCHAR_MAX`/`WINT_MIN`/`WINT_MAX` `unsigned int` (DOCUMENTED in its <stdint.h>: `0U`, `0xffffU`), MSVC types `INT8_MAX` `char` and `UINT16_MAX` `unsigned short` (DOCUMENTED in its <stdint.h>: `127i8`, `0xffffui16`), and every `_MIN` MSVC writes as `(-…iN - 1)` has an `#if` value that disagrees with its C value (MEASURED); both are MEANING forks, decided by C 7.22.5 — the promoted type, which the other pe reference and every ELF one give. `SIG_ATOMIC_*` exist only where `sig_atomic_t` does (C 7.22.3p2: "only the macros corresponding to those typedef names it actually provides"), so they are undefined on pe, where `<signal.h>` is not shipped — exactly the pairs `__SIG_ATOMIC_MAX__` is undefined on (D-C-SIGNAL-H-INCOMPLETE-AND-ABSENT-ON-PE). `__STDC_VERSION_STDINT_H__` is C23 7.22p5 (202311L): no reference defines it yet (glibc 2.39 with gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 13.2.0 and MSVC 14.51 all leave it undefined, MEASURED), and ISO C is part of the union. The C99 7.18.4 `*_C` integer-CONSTANT macros ARE shipped (c39 D-FFI-STDINT-CONSTANT-MACROS). ★ P68 round 9 (found in passing under D-C-LIMITS-H-DEFINES-NINE-OF-THE-STANDARD-MACROS): they used universal `LL`/`ULL` suffixes on the argument that those are >= 64 bits everywhere — true of the WIDTH, but C99 7.18.4p3 (C23 7.22.4p3) gives `INTN_C(v)` the TYPE an `int_leastN_t` has after promotion and `INTMAX_C(v)` the type `intmax_t`, and those are `long` on ELF. So the suffix now follows the typedef's IDENTITY per format: `INT64_C`/`UINT64_C` are `v##L`/`v##UL` on ELF and `v##LL`/`v##ULL` on Mach-O and pe; `INTMAX_C`/`UINTMAX_C` are `v##L`/`v##UL` on ELF and Mach-O (Darwin's `intmax_t` is `long`) and `v##LL`/`v##ULL` on pe. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 by `_Generic`: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (x86_64 Linux, aarch64 Linux under qemu, and gcc natively on the arm64 VPS) give `long`/`unsigned long` for all four; mingw-w64 13.2.0 and MSVC 14.51 give `long long`/`unsigned long long`. The Mach-O arms follow the typedef identities P48 measured on the Mac (recorded below) — INFERRED until the Mac identity probe of this round reports. SQLite uses UINT64_C heavily for 64-bit bitmask constants. * D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY: the 64-bit aliases are no longer a bare `u64`/`i64`. C defines each as an ALIAS of a standard NAMED type, and WHICH name that is depends on the platform. A bare core mints the ANONYMOUS representative, which since type identity was split off representation is a THIRD type matching NEITHER named entry: `stdc_count_ones((uint64_t)x)` fell out of <stdbit.h>'s 5-way `_Generic`, and `unsigned long long *p = &u64var;` became a bare S_TypeMismatch. Each therefore carries a variant selector plus the hir-text vocabulary tag - the SAME 8-byte core everywhere, a different IDENTITY. ** D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-TYPE-ALIAS-SPELLING-KEYED-ON-DATA-MODEL-ALONE: that selector USED TO BE `when:{dataModel}` ALONE, on this file's own stated assumption that `uint64_t`/`uintptr_t`/`uintmax_t`/`size_t` ARE `unsigned long` on LP64 and `unsigned long long` on LLP64 (glibc vs mingw/MSVC). THAT IS A TWO-WORLD ASSUMPTION AND THERE IS A THIRD WORLD. MEASURED 2026-09-01 (P48 lane st) by a `_Generic` compile-only probe - each alias tested against every candidate named type, so the COMPILER's post-typedef-chain answer is read rather than a grep of headers - on the operator's Mac (macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83, MacOSX26.5.sdk, Apple clang 21.0.0, BOTH `-arch arm64` AND `-arch x86_64`, answers byte-identical), against WSL gcc 13.3.0 + clang 18.1.3 + aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc on elf, and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 + MSVC 19.51.36252 on pe: DARWIN IS LP64 AND ITS `uint64_t` IS `unsigned long long` WHILE ITS `size_t` STAYS `unsigned long`, so the aliases the old key held TOGETHER SPLIT and one `dataModel` axis cannot express it. The exact/least/fast-64 six (`int64_t`/`uint64_t`/`int_least64_t`/`uint_least64_t`/`int_fast64_t`/`uint_fast64_t`) are `long long`/`unsigned long long` on macho but `long`/`unsigned long` on elf; the pointer/greatest-width four (`intptr_t`/`uintptr_t`/`intmax_t`/`uintmax_t`) are `long`/`unsigned long` on BOTH elf and macho; all ten are `long long`/`unsigned long long` on pe. Every one of them is 8 bytes on all three platforms, so NOTHING miscompiled by size - what Darwin recorded was a false ABI SPELLING, i.e. a wrong IDENTITY. => every arm now names BOTH axes, `when:{dataModel,format}`. `format` is DSS's per-OS axis (the object format IS the per-OS artifact - see core/types/data_model.hpp; `sys/types.json` already keys `off_t` as `long` on elf and `long long` on macho exactly this way, so this is the established vocabulary rather than a new one), and `dataModel` STAYS in the conjunction because dropping it would let a future ILP32 elf target MATCH the elf arm and silently bind an 8-byte `unsigned long` where the platform's is 4. No ILP32 arm and no fourth-format arm is declared, deliberately: an ILP32 target needs 4-byte intptr/ptrdiff/size widths anyway (D-FFI-STDINT-PTR-WIDTH-ILP32, still open), and an unmeasured platform must never inherit glibc's spelling by default - so 0 variants match there and a reference fails LOUD as an undefined type rather than silently binding a wrong identity.

typedefs.name: int_fast16_t
typedefs.$comment: P68 round 9 (MEASURED 2026-09-23, _Generic + sizeof): the FAST 16/32-bit types are the platform C library's choice, not a width rule. glibc says `long` for int_fast16_t AND int_fast32_t (and `unsigned long` for the unsigned twins) on x86_64 and aarch64, under gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 alike; Darwin (Apple clang 21.0.0, arm64 and x86_64) and mingw-w64 13.2.0 say `short`/`int` (MSVC 14.51 says int/int, but the pe pair presents mingw's identity, so mingw's). This row said i16/i32 on EVERY format, so on the ELF pairs `sizeof(int_fast16_t)` was 2 where glibc's is 8 — an ABI mismatch with every glibc-compiled object that stores one. `__INT_FAST16_TYPE__` & co. name this row, so they follow it.
